Benigno M, Anastassopoulos KP, Mostaghimi A, Udall M, Daniel SR, Cappelleri JC, Chander P, Wahl PM, Lapthorn J, Kauffman L, Chen L, Peeva E, 'A Large Cross-Sectional Survey Study of the Prevalence of Alopecia Areata in the United States', Clin Cosmet Investig Dermatol 2020;13:259-266, doi 10.2147/CCID.S245649, PMID 32280257, PMC7131990: 'Clinician-adjudicated point prevalence of AA was 0.21% (95% CI: 0.17%, 0.25%) overall, 0.12% (95% CI: 0.09%, 0.15%) for "mild" disease (<=50% SALT score), and 0.09% (95% CI: 0.06%, 0.11%) for "moderate to severe" disease (>50% SALT score) with 0.04% (95% CI: 0.02%, 0.06%) for the alopecia totalis/alopecia universalis (100% SALT score) "moderate to severe" subgroup'. The self-reported arm of the same study, 18 cases in the full sample of 45,016, gives the same 0.04%. The survey was census-balanced on US residents aged 11 and over, so the rate is applied to the 297,156,520 US residents aged 11 and over at 1 July 2024 (Census Bureau Vintage 2024, nc-est2024-agesex-res, both sexes, single years of age 11 to 100 summed; the same file gives the 340,110,988 total the book's other rows carry). 0.0004 x 297,156,520 = 118,863
column12: the row does not claim a count for alopecia universalis on its own: no free US source splitting it from alopecia totalis was found, so it reads high. The clinician-adjudicated arm rests on four adjudicated cases and the stated interval, 0.02% to 0.06%, spans 59,431 to 178,294 patients, which is the honest width. No incidence row is written: Benigno is a point-prevalence survey and reports none, and the one US incidence paper found (Kang IE, Strunk A, Garg A, J Am Acad Dermatol 2024;90(1):162-165, doi 10.1016/j.jaad.2023.09.012, PMID 37690704) is a research letter with no free text and no abstract

Sun LD, Behl A, Danilov PN et al., 'Healthcare Resource Utilization and Use of Biologics in Chronic Spontaneous Urticaria', J Dermatol 2026;53(5):832-836 (doi 10.1111/1346-8138.70234, PMID 41934167, PMC13150668), Veterans Health Administration Corporate Data Warehouse, January 2011 to December 2021: 'The final cohort included 26 387 Veterans with CSU. In the 12 month post-index period, 23 699 Veterans (89.8%) started treatment, but only 613 Veterans (2.6%) started biologic therapy, with a median initiation time of 337 days.' 2.6% is the share of all diagnosed chronic spontaneous urticaria patients who reach a systemic agent, which is what this layer's eligible pool is: pfe_litfulo.csv's prevalence is diagnosed disease in an EHR population (Wertenteil 2019) and its eligible_pct of 0.779141 cuts only for inducible urticaria, not for antihistamine failure. So the refractoriness narrowing has to live here, and this row carries it
column12: THE SPREAD ON THIS NUMBER IS 2.6% TO 25% AND THE SPREAD IS DENOMINATOR, NOT MEASUREMENT. The alternative anchor is Mosnaim G, Hetherington J, Keal A, Holden M, Seetasith A, 'Specialist care improves diagnosis and treatment for patients with chronic spontaneous urticaria: A real-world survey', J Allergy Clin Immunol Glob 2025;5(1):100573 (doi 10.1016/j.jacig.2025.100573, PMID 41210911, PMC12590425), Adelphi Real World CSU Disease-Specific Programme, US, December 2020 to October 2021, 120 physicians and 1,082 patients: omalizumab use was 150 (36%) of 414 allergist-managed patients, 96 (21%) of 466 dermatologist-managed and 20 (10%) of 202 PCP-managed. Its denominator is patients actively consulting a physician about urticaria, about 80% specialist-managed by design, which is a far narrower and richer population than a claims-diagnosed one. The low figure is taken because the pool above is claims-diagnosed. WHICH WAY 2.6% ERRS. LOW, on three counts the paper names itself: the window is only the first 12 months after diagnosis and the median time to a biologic in it was 337 days, so it truncates; the authors write 'Studies performed in different patient populations show a higher rate of biologic use (8%-33%)' and 'more patients may have been prescribed biologics at a later date'; and ritlecitinib is oral, where every agent measured here is injected, so it should reach past the biologic segment. HIGH, on one count that is new and material: this segment is no longer omalizumab's alone. Dupixent was approved for 'Chronic Spontaneous Urticaria ... in adult and pediatric patients aged 2 years and older ... who remain symptomatic despite H1 antihistamine treatment' (DailyMed setid 595f437d-2729-40bb-9c62-c8ece1f82780, SPL version 60, 2026-08-07), and the book's own BLU-808 row carries a 0.016365 anchor solved on Rhapsido's launch. Three mechanisms now compete for the same refractory patients and this row claims the whole measured biologic segment for a fourth
